title: Jane the Superpredictor
disclosure: Illustrative devnet walkthrough. Election and council-document scenarios are hypothetical. No investment returns are guaranteed.

scenes.visual: Actual UGT planet or global map view, moving toward a city. Do not add fake markers.
scenes.narration: Jane is a planet surfer. She loves exploring our blue marble. Opinionated, well informed, and always monitoring the situation. We call her a Superpredictor.

scenes.visual: Actual proposal list and a real apartment-block proposal in Zagreb if available. Keep its lifecycle and parcel details legible; retain the subtle illustrative-devnet label.
scenes.narration: On a typical day, Jane opens Urban Game Theory and scrolls the latest proposals. A new apartment block in Zagreb catches her eye. She clicks.

scenes.visual: Show the actual 3D view and design of the apartment-block proposal with surrounding streets. Do not add or imply a park footprint.
scenes.narration: The three-dimensional view brings it to life. New homes, on these parcels, in this neighbourhood. It looks good. But Jane knows something the picture cannot tell her.

scenes.visual: Use the supplied code-drawn concept clip labeled 'ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIO'. It shows only the hypothetical possibility that an opposing party may win; it contains no poll, result, number, source, or app card. Do not present it as real election evidence.
scenes.narration: In this example, the party promising to block the project is leading the next election. Jane thinks execution is unlikely. That suggests a NO bet.

scenes.visual: Actual apartment-block proposal details: resolution lens/evidence, funds, pledges, donations, and owner acceptance progress. Show only visible real values.
scenes.narration: First, she checks who will resolve the outcome. Does she trust that lens? Then the details: money committed, pledges, donations, and parcel-owner acceptances. Every signal can change her view.

scenes.visual: Actual YES/NO market and stake flow, or an already existing devnet position. No new stake transaction is needed; do not fabricate a wallet receipt.
scenes.narration: Her conclusion holds. Jane selects NO, chooses her stake, and confirms. The stake stays locked until resolution. Cancellation or recorded expiry pays NO; execution pays YES.

scenes.visual: Use the real public park proposal list only to establish the identity and nearby two-parcel context for UPU Borovje – javni park Z1-3 (published and unminted). Follow it with the supplied separate illustrative donation concept. The public proposal has no shown completed donation or conditional funds; do not imply it received Jane's hypothetical donation. No wallet flow, receipt, success state, or transaction.
scenes.narration: Then she spots another proposal nearby: buy two parcels and make a public park. Jane wants that to happen. She donates fifty dollars in devnet USDC.

scenes.visual: Use the supplied code-drawn conditional refund diagram. It explains a one-year path only; it does not depict a real proposal already Expired or a completed transaction/claim. In an actual case, expiry must be recorded on-chain before a donor can claim.
scenes.narration: The donation sits in escrow. This plan needs all parcel owners to accept. If it has not executed after a year, and expiry is recorded on-chain, Jane can claim her donation back.

scenes.visual: Return to the actual UGT globe or global map. Keep a genuine proposal/lifecycle marker visible if one is part of the application.
scenes.narration: A forecast on one project. Support for another. Jane returns to happily surfing the planet. Urban Game Theory. Explore your world, predict what changes, and help shape what comes next.
